_comment: Ratchet for bun run test:audit. Counts normally only go down: lower a number in the same commit that lowers the count. A number may go UP only when the DETECTOR got stricter and started seeing sites that were always there, never to admit new ones — raise it in the same commit as the detector change and record the reason below.
_wallClock: 0. The last ten sites went in one pass (see the PR that lowered this line). Each became either a BRACKET — two clock readings taken either side of the call, so the stamp is pinned to an instant inside them and no tolerance encodes machine speed — an EVENT ORDER (the estimator is released only after the route has answered; a shutdown marker due before the drain's own timer, which the event loop therefore always fires first), a WAIT rather than an assertion (the review-item precondition loops until the clock leaves the stamped millisecond, which slowness only makes arrive sooner), or a COUNT in the style of list-docs-linear.test.ts (paragraph re-scans, round trips, eager binds). Nothing was deleted to reach zero: every rewrite was shown red against a deliberately broken timing. A number here may go UP only if the detector gets stricter.
_sourceShape:
12. Was 42, and 42 was never a census (the history of why is in the PR that raised it from 36: the detector got stricter and surfaced six reads that were always there).

THE MCP PASS (42 -> 30). The nine MCP tests that read packages/mcp/src through test/harness/mcp-source.ts drive the built bundle over stdio instead — claim-warning, decision-line, declare-lead, nudge-line, plugin-version-reported, review-item-tools, stale-write-surface, tool-wiring, watch-coverage. The harness they used is deleted, not exempted. Every rewrite was shown red against a deliberately broken bundle, and SIX of the old source assertions stayed GREEN under the same break; two more were FALSE POSITIVES on a behaviour-preserving respelling. packages/widget/test/css-minify.test.ts carries a per-site `// audit: not-source` marker: styles.css there is the minifier's INPUT, not the subject. That third shape is written into the marker's docstring in scripts/test-audit.ts, with the discriminator a reviewer applies.

THE WORKSPACES-APP PASS (30 -> 12). Twelve suites in packages/workspaces-app/test stopped reading src/board/*.ts, app.ts, board-live-wiring.ts and meeting-strip.ts as text and boot the real thing instead: lazy-events and load-beacon (PR 731), then board-mic-dock-css, board-model, board-quick-actions, board-source-contract, home-board-rows, home-nav-reset, meeting-strip-css (its meeting-strip.ts half), parallelism-cap, review-criteria, review-item-comments.tsx, walk-handoff and walk-return. The shared driver is test/support/board-drive.ts — one bootBoard against the boot-harness fakes, with the queue, the address and the fetches read back. EIGHTEEN deliberate breaks were run, each against the converted assertion AND against a replica of the assertion it replaced. In SIXTEEN of the eighteen the old assertion stayed GREEN. The ones worth naming, because they say what this class of test was actually worth:
  - home-nav-reset: all four old assertions stayed green — including the one named 'closes it even when Home is already the destination' — with exactly that bug reintroduced.
  - board-source-contract: a second createVoiceCapture mounted from board-live-wiring.ts, outside the grep's file list, left the old count at 1 while one Space press started TWO recognizers.
  - walk-handoff: burning the one-shot walk flag on a not-ready queue left all eight old assertions green, 'an empty queue leaves the flag armed until the deadline' among them.
  - review-item-comments: the old ABSENCE assertion ('no walkHold, no holdWaitingItem, no waiting copy') stayed green while the held-card bug it is named after was reinstated, because nothing brought those identifiers back. Absence greps on identifiers do not survive a rename in either direction.
  - board-mic-dock-css: the mic's aria-label is a RUNTIME value that depends on isSecureContext, so reading it out of a template literal was never the same assertion.
The two breaks an old assertion DID catch are recorded in the PR body: reinstating the held card moved a line one regex pinned by adjacency, and an early attempt at the board-model break left the literal it greps for inside a function body the regex reads.

THE FLOOR IS 3, and they are named: decide-option-hover-css.test.ts (a :hover treatment), board-nav-widget-clearance-css.test.ts (a calc() of max() and env() happy-dom discards whole) and shell-grid-placement.test.ts (grid auto-placement, which needs a layout engine). They are PERMANENT and counted, not exempted. bun run ui:shot would render them for real, but it is a local dev tool — it needs a Chrome binary and a running server, and .github/workflows/ci.yml does not run it — so moving them there would retire the checks rather than convert them. Each file says so in its own header. If ui:shot ever runs in CI, convert them and take this to 0.

WHAT REMAINS ABOVE THE FLOOR — 9 sites in 4 files, each left as it is rather than marked or weakened:
  - board-url-wiring.test.ts (2): the boot's codec calls and app.ts's revealLinkedThread. Most of this file is driveable through board-drive.ts and was simply not reached this pass; one test in it ('renders the open before the walkthrough close') says in its own comment that it pins SHAPE and that nothing in this repo can test the race it stands for.
  - huddle-entry.test.ts (2): app.ts decides a huddle started here and doc/doc-meeting-mount.ts acts on it. mountMarkdown runs per doc, not per page, so no harness here boots it.
  - meeting-strip-css.test.ts (1): the same per-doc mount decision (docType === 'markdown').
  - sentry-boot.test.ts (2): 'neither entry imports @sentry/browser' is a claim about what ends up in a BUNDLE. A module-graph probe would catch a static import and MISS a dynamic one inside an uncalled function, which is the case the assertion exists for — so it stays a source read until a build-output check can stand behind it.

Still invisible, so nobody reads 12 as a census either: a read whose path is in a constant declared elsewhere (review-item-tools.test.ts still reads a BUNDLE const that way), a support module outside a test/ directory, and require().
